h1: Landscaping & lawn care in Big Sandy
lede: Big Sandy is out US 80 past Gladewater, in the southwest part of Upshur County. We take care of lawns, beds, drainage, patios and Christmas lights for homes in town and on the acreage around it.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned landscaping and lawn care company out of Longview, and Big Sandy is in our Upshur County service area. Miller Maines founded the company in 2017. The crew is Miller and four others, the same people every visit, and we never sub the work out. We are fully insured and hold a 5.0 rating from {{REVIEWS}} Google reviews. Send a quote request any time for a free walkthrough and a written, itemized estimate, usually within a day.

The town takes its name from Big Sandy Creek, and the name fits the ground. The soil around here is mostly sand, deep in places, with clay underneath in the low spots. It drains fast on the high ground and stays wet in the creek bottoms. A lot of homes sit on an acre or several, with pines and hardwoods along the edges and open lawn in between. Lawns burn up quickly in a dry August, and beds need help holding water.

Big Sandy is an easy drive west from our shop on US 80, so it works for weekly mowing as well as bigger installs. Acreage changes the job, so we walk the property before we price it and look at the trim work, the fence lines and where water runs after a rain. If you live between Big Sandy and Hawkins or up toward Gilmer, send your address with a quote request and we will confirm it is in range.

yard_notes.title: Sand up high, wet down low
yard_notes.text: Yards on higher ground drain in hours and dry out fast in summer. Near the creek and in low pockets, clay under the sand keeps water sitting after a heavy rain.

yard_notes.title: Acreage means trim work
yard_notes.text: Many homes sit on an acre or more. Fence lines, outbuildings and long drives add trim time, and that is what moves the mowing price more than open turf.

yard_notes.title: Tree lines and open middles
yard_notes.text: Pines and hardwoods ring a lot of lots, with open sun in the middle. That is Bermuda in the open and St. Augustine only where the shade is real.

yard_notes.title: Leaves blow in from the edges
yard_notes.text: The tree line drops needles and leaves onto the lawn edges and beds every fall, and the wind spreads them across the open yard.

faq.q: Does Yard Dog work in Big Sandy?
faq.a: Yes. Big Sandy is out US 80 west of Gladewater, and it is part of our Upshur County service area. We do mowing, beds, sod, drainage, patios, retaining walls and Christmas lights out here. Send your address with a quote request, and we will set up a free walkthrough.

faq.q: How do you price mowing on acreage in Big Sandy?
faq.a: A typical residential yard starts at $65 per visit for weekly mowing. On an acre or more, the price depends on how much is open turf versus fence line, outbuildings and trim work. We walk it and give you a flat per-visit price in writing.

faq.q: Part of my yard stays wet for days after rain. Is that normal here?
faq.a: It is common in the low spots around Big Sandy, where sand sits on a clay layer. Water drains through the sand, hits the clay and spreads out. A regrade, swale or French drain usually fixes it. Most drainage projects run $2,000 to $3,750, with small fixes starting around $450.

faq.q: What do Christmas lights cost in Big Sandy?
faq.a: Most homes start at $900. We supply the lights, custom-cut professional C9 lines to the roofline, install them, take them down after the season and store them. We quote from a photo mock-up, so you can text us a picture and get a number without waiting on a visit.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: Big Sandy lawns are often big and open, with fence lines, outbuildings and a long drive to work around. We mow the turf at the right height for the grass, string-trim the fence lines and buildings, edge the drive and walks, and blow the clippings back into the lawn instead of bagging them. Weekly mowing starts at $65 a visit for a typical yard, and acreage is priced after we walk it.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Country lots around Big Sandy collect leaves and needles from the tree line every fall, and the wind pushes them across the open lawn and into the beds. We mulch the light early drop with the mower and switch to full cleanup when the volume starts burying the grass, clearing beds, drives and fence lines too. Leaf removal is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.fertilization: On a big Big Sandy lot, it rarely makes sense to feed every acre. We focus the program on the lawn you see and use, test the soil first, and follow the four-step East Texas schedule from late April to a late October winterizer, with slow-release product so it feeds the grass instead of washing through the sand. Fertilization starts from about $190 per visit.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: Around Big Sandy, hedges tend to be either foundation shrubs on the house or long screens along a property line. We shape both so the base stays full, cut hollies and ligustrum in early summer after the spring flush, and keep big screens at a height you can live with. Most hedge jobs run $150 to $800, and we haul off every clipping.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: On wooded lots near Big Sandy, the work is mostly about the trees and shrubs near the house: dead lower limbs, crepe myrtles that need thinning instead of topping, and shrubs that have crept over walks and beds. We prune each plant in its right window and remove small trees and overgrown shrubs. This work is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.tree-planting: Big open lots around Big Sandy have room for real shade trees: oaks and southern magnolias want open space and ground that drains, while a bald cypress or river birch can handle a wetter low area. We plant October through February when we can, set the root flare at grade, and leave you a watering plan for the root ball. Tree planting is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.sod-installation: On a big lot, sodding the whole thing is rarely needed, and we usually recommend sodding the front and the area around the house where it shows and gets used. Bermuda is the pick in open sun, and St. Augustine goes where the shade is real. Sod is priced by the pallet, and most projects run $1,500 to $4,700.
service_angles.landscaping: On a country property near Big Sandy, landscaping usually means framing the house so it looks finished against a big open yard: foundation beds, a couple of trees, and clean edges between lawn and bed. We plant for heat and sand and keep the layout simple to maintain. Most projects run $900 to $3,600, and smaller refreshes start at a few hundred dollars.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: Big Sandy beds on open lots take full afternoon sun, so we plant what likes it: lantana, salvia, plumbago and annual vinca, which goes in once the soil warms up in mid-May. Compost goes in first so the sand holds water between rains. Most planting projects run $900 to $3,600, and a $199 flower bed Design Preview can lay out the bed before we dig.
service_angles.mulch-installation: Some country homes around Big Sandy run rock along the foundation and mulch everywhere else, and that split makes sense: rock gets landscape fabric under it, mulch does not. We lay hardwood 1 to 1.5 inches deep over a clean, edged bed so it breaks down and feeds the sand underneath. Most bed refreshes run $600 to $2,400.
service_angles.hardscaping: Out on bigger lots around Big Sandy, a patio often sits off the back porch with a fire pit a few steps out into the yard. We build both on a compacted crushed stone base, lock the edges so loose sand cannot creep, and pitch the patio away from the house. Most patio and hardscape projects run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: Where a Big Sandy lot drops toward a creek or a ditch, soil can wash out with every heavy rain, and a low block or stone wall holds the grade and makes room for a flat bed or patio. We build every wall on a compacted base with gravel backfill and a drain behind it. Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000 by height and length.
service_angles.drainage: Big Sandy drainage problems tend to sit at the bottom of the lot: the low corner near the creek or ditch, or the side of the house where a downspout dumps into flat sand over clay. We regrade, build swales and dry creek beds, and install French drains that outlet to daylight or a pop-up emitter. Most projects run $2,000 to $3,750, and small fixes start around $450.
service_angles.christmas-lights: Big Sandy is well inside our Christmas light range, and most homes start at $900. Long rooflines get C9 lines custom-cut to fit, installed, taken down after the season and stored until next year, in warm white or color. We quote from a photo mock-up, so a picture of the house is all we need to get started.
service_angles.irrigation: Big Sandy earns its name: deep sand that takes water fast and gives it up fast. We water the part of the property you actually use, zone it by sun and shade, and put beds on drip, rather than trying to irrigate acreage that does fine on rain.

lawn-maintenance.q: Can you mow just the area around my house on a big lot?
lawn-maintenance.a: Yes. On acreage, we can keep the lawn around the house, the drive and the nearby fence lines sharp and leave the outer ground alone. We price only the area we mow and trim, in writing, after a walkthrough.

leaf-removal.q: Do you clear leaves out of beds and fence lines too?
leaf-removal.a: Yes. A full cleanup covers the lawn, beds, walks, drive and fence lines, and we haul the leaves off. On wooded lots the tree line keeps dropping into December, so a second pass is often worth scheduling.

fertilization.q: Is it worth fertilizing a whole acre?
fertilization.a: Usually not. We focus feedings on the lawn you see and use, around the house and out front, and leave the outer ground alone. That keeps the cost in check and puts the product where it shows. Fertilization starts from about $190 per visit.

hedge-trimming.q: How often should a privacy hedge be trimmed?
hedge-trimming.a: Once a year is the minimum for most hollies, ligustrum and wax myrtles, in early summer after the spring flush. Fast growers may need a second, lighter trim in early fall. Waiting several years means a hard cut that leaves the hedge thin for a season.

tree-shrub-care.q: Can you clear small trees and overgrown shrubs around the house?
tree-shrub-care.a: Yes. We remove small trees and overgrown shrubs that have outgrown their spot, prune what stays, and haul off the debris. Big trees, especially near the house, are a job for a tree service, and we will tell you when that is the case.

tree-planting.q: What trees grow in a wet spot near the creek?
tree-planting.a: Bald cypress and river birch both handle wet feet better than most trees. Oaks and magnolias want ground that drains. We check how long water sits after a rain before we pick a tree for a low spot.

sod-installation.q: When is the best time to lay sod in Big Sandy?
sod-installation.a: Bermuda goes down best from late April through August, and St. Augustine from May through September, when the ground is warm. We avoid dry stretches when you cannot water every day, because deep morning watering for the first two weeks decides whether it takes.

landscaping.q: Can you make a country house look finished without a lot of upkeep?
landscaping.a: Yes. We keep beds close to the house, use shrubs that hold their shape, add a couple of trees for shade and scale, and cut clean edges so mowing stays simple. Fewer, bigger beds are easier to keep up than lots of small ones. Most projects run $900 to $3,600.

flower-bed-installation.q: When is the best time to plant flower beds in Big Sandy?
flower-bed-installation.a: Shrubs and perennials do best planted in fall, when the soil is still warm and roots keep growing through winter. Heat lovers like vinca wait until the soil warms up in mid-May. Spring planting works too, but new beds need more water through their first summer.

mulch-installation.q: Should I use rock or mulch in my beds?
mulch-installation.a: Rock works along foundations and in drainage channels, and it gets fabric under it. Mulch is better in planted beds, because it breaks down and feeds the soil, and it should never have fabric under it. We lay hardwood 1 to 1.5 inches deep over a clean, edged bed.

hardscaping.q: How much does a patio and fire pit cost in Big Sandy?
hardscaping.a: Most patio and hardscape projects run $3,100 to $9,100, depending on size, material and access. We walk the spot, talk through pavers versus flagstone, and send a written, itemized estimate. If you want to see it first, our hardscape Design Preview is $449 and is credited toward the build if you book within 90 days.

retaining-walls.q: What does a small retaining wall cost?
retaining-walls.a: Short garden walls start at a few thousand dollars. Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000 depending on height and length, and tall structural walls can pass $20,000. We price each one after walking the slope, because the base and drainage behind the wall are a big part of the work.

drainage.q: Can you fix water standing near my house in Big Sandy?
drainage.a: Usually, yes. We find where the water comes from, then regrade the soil away from the slab, reroute downspouts, or run a French drain to a daylighted outlet. Small fixes run about $450 to $1,000, and most full projects run $2,000 to $3,750.

christmas-lights.q: Can you light a long ranch-style roofline?
christmas-lights.a: Yes. We custom-cut C9 lines to the exact roofline, long runs included, in warm white or color. Most homes start at $900, and we take everything down after the season and store it until next year.

irrigation.q: Do you install sprinkler systems in Big Sandy?
irrigation.a: Yes. We install and repair sprinkler systems in Big Sandy and out toward Hawkins, under a Texas licensed irrigator, and pull the permit the job requires. Pricing comes after a free walkthrough.
